claim: The checked-in default contains two independent Crystal Lattice Claude-compatible profiles: a direct Anthropic Messages route and an OpenRouter route, both using local Claude prompt/tool packages rather than official Claude Code sessions.
verification_method: Pinned config/source inspection plus focused provider and tool tests.
verification_result: 58 Anthropic and 84 Claude-tools tests passed independently; OpenRouter deterministic coverage also passed.
limitations: No hosted Anthropic/OpenRouter request, account entitlement, or official-product interoperability was verified.
Default-config prompt/runtime loading has a separate local plugin-cache verification gap.

claim: The checked-in default contains three Codex-oriented Crystal Lattice profiles with materially different OpenAI auto-auth, explicit API-key, and OpenRouter routes; they are not official Codex sessions.
verification_method: Config/source review, model/prompt probes, Codex selection tests, provider/auth unit tests, and client-source review.
verification_result: Codex shell-selection, prompt selection, provider/auth, cost, packaging, and frontend tests passed locally; no hosted route was run.
limitations: OpenAI auto auth changes effective route based on saved credentials.
OpenRouter capabilities depend on live model discovery.
No official session/account parity is established.

claim: The two GPT-5 profiles deliberately use array-form shell with intercepted patch handling rather than the shell-command tool shape used by later Codex-oriented profiles.
verification_method: Resolved config/source inspection and direct shell-selection regression tests.
verification_result: Focused Codex model-family/tool-selection suite passed.
limitations: No hosted GPT-5 request or effective production-session tool schema was verified.
OpenAI and OpenRouter account/capability states remain route-specific.

claim: Qwen, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, and GLM are configured OpenRouter-backed compatibility profiles whose prompt/tool composition differs by profile; GLM uses Gemini behavior and Grok composes Grok and residual Qwen tools.
verification_method: Pinned config/descriptor/source review and focused OpenRouter capability/tool/reasoning/usage/web tests.
verification_result: 80 focused OpenRouter tests passed independently; model-family package suites exposed current failures/timeouts and remain incomplete.
limitations: Descriptor entries do not prove effective live schemas or model tool acceptance.
Search/media paths require additional credentials or capability flags.
No official upstream parity is established.

claim: The reference-compatible profiles share one generic OpenAI-compatible provider implementation but differ in route, model identifier, prompt/tool package, request settings, and prerequisites; Ollama :cloud model names still use the configured localhost endpoint.
verification_method: Pinned config/provider/tool inspection and reproduced provider-extension tests.
verification_result: 121 focused reference-provider tests passed independently; local Ollama and hosted Fireworks/Z.ai gates were not run.
limitations: A :cloud suffix does not prove remote execution, account entitlement, or local weight placement.
Configured request options do not prove endpoint acceptance.

claim: The default includes specialist profiles for authoring cloud project hooks and for non-streaming OpenRouter image generation; neither profile proves cloud infrastructure or hosted image availability.
verification_method: Config/source review plus focused cloud, image-provider, attachment, builder, and SDK tests.
verification_result: 9 image tests, 12 focused cloud-plugin tests, 12 cloud bundle/source tests, and related SDK tests passed.
limitations: No hosted image response, Docker, orchestrator, SSH, transfer, deployment, or produced artifact was exercised.

claim: FastAPI and the production frontend SDK provide the strongest shared client contract; mobile and desktop consume broad generic schemas/actions, while terminal console and standalone CLI/Python expose different, narrower workflows.
verification_method: Production-source trace plus real local FastAPI/FetchTransport/RestAgentBackend integration and focused client tests.
verification_result: Backend integration passed 21/21 on warm-cache retry after an initial 19-pass/2-startup-timeout run; status and action-display integrations passed; frontend/mobile/desktop unit suites passed.
limitations: Native mobile/macOS UI suites were not run.
Generic consumer support does not establish every conditional plugin control or provider-specific workflow.
HTTP event streaming is polling, not SSE/websocket.

claim: Cost, usage, message duration, and human-time data are separate route- and plugin-dependent surfaces; values may be provider-reported, locally estimated, API-equivalent, or unavailable and must not be presented uniformly as bills.
verification_method: Source review plus focused cost/duration/usage tests and client metadata review.
verification_result: Cost, duration, timestamp, and route-specific unit/integration slices passed locally; no provider invoice comparison was made.
limitations: Pricing snapshots and configured token rates can drift.
Image and Anthropic routes do not share identical cost promotion behavior.
Duration tracking is optional-not-default.

claim: History summaries, native rebuild, assets, exports, compaction, duration reports, timestamp metadata, and sleep prevention have distinct mutation, persistence, selection, and prerequisite boundaries; only summarize, rebuild, assets, and timestamp behavior are selected by the default among these rows.
verification_method: Pinned selection/source review plus focused plugin, core, HTTP, SDK, duration, and mocked OS tests.
verification_result: Core snapshot/asset/projection/notification and most plugin/client slices passed; export remained timeout-incomplete after dependencies were installed.
limitations: Provider-backed summarization/compaction was not run.
Export browser/pandoc/SMTP/Keychain/native-share paths remain unverified.
Generic snapshot/projection behavior is not attributed to one plugin.

claim: Provider packages are globally selected and implement different discovery, authentication, request, tool, reasoning, attachment, usage, caching, and compaction contracts; package presence does not make those capabilities uniform.
verification_method: Descriptor/source review and focused provider/extension unit tests.
verification_result: Anthropic, OpenAI Responses, OpenRouter, and reference-compatible deterministic suites passed in their inspected slices.
limitations: No current hosted availability, account entitlement, provider acceptance, or universal frontend parity was verified.

claim: Ten default-selected application plugins jointly provide session mutation, titles, bounded main search, counts, pin/archive/status metadata, timestamps, filters, and plugin-derived ordering through the shared SessionListService and API contracts.
verification_method: Source/config review plus public HTTP, core application, SDK, React, and plugin tests.
verification_result: Public HTTP 5/5, core list/filter/app-plugin 33/33, and SDK/React slices passed; combined plugin slice retained four failures and one deselection.
limitations: Main search does not search all messages; client fallback is narrower.
Generated title requires a provider request.
Generic terminal action execution and native UI verification remain incomplete.

claim: Cloud actions, image generation, and session assets are implemented as separate layers: cloud operations require project/orchestrator/transfer infrastructure, image conversion is provider-specific, and generic assets provide storage/download plumbing.
verification_method: Source review plus image, asset, cloud-plugin, builder, embedded-runtime, and SDK tests.
verification_result: Focused local slices passed; no Docker/remote/provider/native artifact was run.
limitations: Builder inputs are not produced artifact parity.
Generic assets do not prove provider acceptance or terminal attachment UI.

claim: The default selects broad schema/action-based configuration and transparency features, while duration tracking is optional-not-default and common Codex/Claude MCP defaults are disabled.
verification_method: Pinned config/source review and focused tool-gating, request-options, system-message, context, config, MCP, cost, duration, API, and client tests.
verification_result: Most focused slices passed; ChatGPT-auth selections timed out and remain incomplete.
limitations: Schema/action availability is conditional by provider/session.
No credentials, remote web fetch, MCP server, or hosted account flow was exercised.
Terminal/headless action support remains a separate contradiction.

claim: Five checked-in GPT-5 or GPT-5.4-mini Codex-family profiles select the generic GPT-5 prompt, which states that update_plan is available, but the selected Codex descriptor/direct probe does not register it; codex-openai-api selects a distinct GPT-5.4 prompt and is not included.
verification_method: Prompt-selection reproduction, descriptor/source-tree comparison, and direct configured-class probe.
verification_result: The five affected profiles selected the GPT-5 prompt; the direct Codex probe exposed shell and apply_patch schemas but no update_plan. Reference subagent/request-input schemas were not descriptor entries.
limitations: A higher runtime layer could inject additional tools, but no default selected path was established.
This is a prompt/tool contract mismatch, not a provider capability claim.

claim: Several focused tests disagree with current source/public behavior: Grok declares bash while tests expect it absent, application UI schema adds order metadata a plugin test omits, event-store tests use an outdated result shape, and unknown-agent session deletion raises during lifecycle resolution.
verification_method: Source/test comparison and bounded failing-test review.
verification_result: Contradictions reproduced or retained from exact packet commands; challenge verification pending final synthesis.
limitations: Not every failing test is user-visible product failure.
Catalog wording must follow public/source behavior while preserving unresolved edge-case risk.

claim: HTTP, SDK, mobile, and desktop generic action execution is established, but no interactive terminal-console or standalone CLI/Python adapter for arbitrary session/application actions has been established.
verification_method: Source/API/client comparison and local action-display integration; narrow challenge pending.
verification_result: HTTP/SDK action routes passed locally; terminal settings/plugins/native commands are present, but generic action execution was not found before challenge completion.
limitations: A contributed standalone application command is not a generic session-action adapter.
Internal Python application methods are not automatically a supported public headless API.

claim: Default-config packaging analysis selects the relevant local plugin closure and builders stage selected projects/resources, but source selection and builder tests do not prove installed bundled-Python, optimized, cloud, or embedded artifact parity.
verification_method: Isolated packaging analysis and focused builder/source-staging tests.
verification_result: Config resolved without fatal errors; selected/local closure extracted; cloud bundle/source staging tests passed.
limitations: No bundled package, optimized archive/executable, cloud image/deployment, or mobile artifact was built or run.

claim: Several explicit privacy boundaries exist—allowlisted secret inputs, token-omitting status projections, and default cloud transfer exclusions—but they do not establish comprehensive secret redaction across every log, cache, history, export, attachment, or project hook.
verification_method: Config/source/privacy-boundary review and focused local tests.
verification_result: Synthetic configuration, MCP, cloud policy, and export-source checks completed; no real credential was read.
limitations: No exhaustive memory/log/idempotency/export/attachment/cloud-path audit was performed.
Optional export and auth lifecycles remain incompletely verified.

claim: The direct Anthropic route uses API-key authentication and native Messages/model-list behavior with configured reasoning controls and prompt caching; no hosted account/model acceptance was verified.
verification_method: Provider source inspection and focused deterministic tests.
verification_result: 58 Anthropic provider/transport/cache/reasoning/tool/usage tests passed independently.
limitations: No real credential, model catalog, beta acceptance, tool request, usage, or account entitlement evidence.

claim: The image route implements a non-streaming OpenRouter request and normalizes generated image data into session assets/multipart output, while usage/cost promotion and hosted availability remain unverified.
verification_method: Source/config review plus focused image provider/attachment and asset tests.
verification_result: 9 image provider/attachment tests and related asset/SDK slices passed.
limitations: No hosted request, account entitlement, current model availability, image result, price, or native UI run.

claim: The OpenAI provider supports materially different API-key and saved-ChatGPT routes; auto mode selects saved ChatGPT when a saved access token exists, and route-specific request/model/cost behavior must remain separate.
verification_method: Source/config review and focused provider/auth/reasoning/usage/cost tests.
verification_result: Deterministic OpenAI Responses and cost/auth slices passed; selected ChatGPT-auth app tests timed out and no login was run.
limitations: No dated hosted result, account entitlement, invoice reconciliation, or native-compaction request.
API-equivalent ChatGPT cost is an estimate.

claim: OpenRouter uses API-key Chat Completions and runtime model discovery; selected-model supported parameters determine important tool/reasoning capability tags, so model names and local descriptors alone do not prove active provider features.
verification_method: Provider/source review and focused capability/tool/reasoning/usage/web/attachment tests.
verification_result: 80 focused and 94 broader OpenRouter deterministic tests passed independently.
limitations: No live /models response, routing fulfillment, selected-model request, account entitlement, or billed-cost evidence.

claim: The reference-compatible provider implements generic Chat Completions discovery, tools, reasoning, attachments, usage/cost, and retry behavior for materially different local Ollama, Fireworks, and Z.ai routes.
verification_method: Pinned route/config/source inspection and focused provider-extension unit tests.
verification_result: 121 reference-provider tests passed independently; local Ollama and hosted Fireworks/Z.ai integrations were not run.
limitations: Generic provider tags and UI are not endpoint acceptance, current pricing, account, local model, or provider-specific client parity.

claim: Checked-in plugin selection and packaging analysis are established, but a clean isolated full-default runtime did not reach complete plugin class instantiation: offline probes stopped earlier at local build-tool prerequisites, so the previously observed generated-cache pydantic_core import symptom remains unresolved rather than proven stale-cache or clean-start product failure.
verification_method: Two fresh copied-config/cache offline runtime probes, host pydantic_core import check, direct-source representative plugin probe, and packaging analysis.
verification_result: Full default instantiation unresolved; offline probes failed on setuptools/wheel build prerequisites before pydantic_core class imports. Host pydantic_core import and direct representative probe succeeded.
limitations: Offline no-index probes do not represent the supported package build path.
Shared caches were not deleted or mutated.
A fresh supported source-install or bundled runtime smoke is still required.
